title: Ebike rider, 13, charged with sexual touching after girls and women allegedly harassed on northern beaches
text:
An ebike riding 13-year-old boy has been charged with multiple sexual offences allegedly committed against women on walking trails on Sydney’s northern beaches.

New South Wales police said the boy was arrested on Saturday evening after a strike force was established to investigate inappropriate comments and alleged sexual touching incidents on walking trails in the Narrabeen area in the first weeks of October.

“Following a public appeal, a 13-year-old boy was arrested after attending Mona Vale police station about 7.30pm yesterday,” police said on Sunday.

The teenager was taken to Manly police station and charged with three counts of behaving in an offensive manner in or near a public place, and eight counts of sexually touching another person without consent.

On Saturday, police had released CCTV images of a male they believed could assist with inquiries.

Police allege that 11 separate incidents occurred against girls and women aged between 13 and 54.

The investigation was initially launched after three separate alleged incidents on 7 and 8 October.

“In each incident, a male allegedly approached women on walking trails, sexually touched them and then rode away on an ebike,” police said on Saturday. In one of the incidents, the offender allegedly made “inappropriate sexual comments”.

At Narrabeen lagoon about 4.30pm on 1 October the suspect “allegedly sexually touched [a] woman before riding away on an ebike,” police said.

Last Monday, police received a further report that between 5pm and 5.30pm that day, two women walking along the Narrabeen lagoon near Bilarong reserve had been sexually touched by a male riding an ebike.

Strike Force Mexvo was established to investigate the incidents with assistance from state crime command’s sex crimes quad.

Speaking in Narrabeen before Saturday’s arrest, Supt John Duncan urged members of the public to come forward with any information about the alleged incidents.

“It’s a bushland park that runs 8km, a large amount of which … runs through bushland, obviously there’s not a great deal of CCTV and cameras.”

The 13-year-old was granted conditional bail to appear at children’s court on 4 November.

title: Plover, not a fighter: protected bird 12th man on Tasmanian cricket ground as staff mow around nest
text:
At Windsor Park in Riverside, just outside Launceston in northern Tasmania, a masked lapwing has claimed prime real estate in the middle of a community sports ground, showing complete indifference to the weekend cricket matches taking place around it.

Warming a nest of eggs, the bird has been affectionately dubbed “Faf Swoop Plessis” by locals – a play on former South African cricket captain Faf du Plessis.

Because the species is protected under state law, carrying fines of up to $21,300 for disturbing nests, ground staff have had to mow around the site, while players steer clear.

During a match early in the season, Great Northern Raiders player Caleb Brewer drew the short straw and was stationed directly beside the nest.

“At the start it was pretty weird, but towards the middle we kind of got used to it and the plover wasn’t too bad at the end,” Brewer told local paper The Examiner.

The next weekend, Riverside first-grade opener Josh Partridge was tasked with fielding near the plover, but reached a peaceful “mutual understanding”, according to The Examiner.

“It was like the plover knew there was a game of cricket going on,” he said. “We weren’t interfering with what was going on in its life, so it didn’t want to interfere with what was going on in ours.”

That kind of sporting truce is common, according to Mark Holdsworth from BirdLife Tasmania.

“Lapwings will often become accustomed to the local patterns of people using a site and in many situations people modify their behaviour to avoid the core nesting area,” Holdsworth said. Everyone has learned to live with each other.”

While masked lapwings – widely known across Australia as plovers – have an intimidating call and reputation for swooping during spring nesting season, choosing a wide-open lawn is actually a calculated survival tactic.

Sports ovals are a “fantastic place” for them to nest, Holdsworth said, because unobstructed views mean parent birds can spot threats early.

Sean Dooley from BirdLife Australia also said that what looks like eccentric behaviour to humans makes sense for plovers.

“The places they choose to nest can seem crazy from our perspective, but there is logic to it,” Dooley said. “They like to nest out in the open so they can see danger coming and they rely on camouflage to hide their eggs and their chicks. So by nesting on an oval, they have a clear view in all directions.”

He said that when people give the bird a wide berth, lapwings generally realise they are not under threat.

“They definitely aren’t out to get us by nature, they really only care about making sure their chicks aren’t being threatened …

“Swooping isn’t their only tactic; they also put on a display that mimics having a broken wing to lure potential threats away. They’re just being good parents and doing all they can to protect their young.”

title: Most NSW homes destroyed in black summer bushfires were within 100 metres of vegetation
text:
Almost every home destroyed in New South Wales during the black summer bushfires of 2019-20 was inside the 100 metre buffer zone used to identify properties most at risk, new research has found.

The findings are an endorsement of the risk maps used by authorities, but the research warns that as global heating generates ever-worsening fire conditions, firefighters may have to extend the recommended distances between homes and vegetation to keep properties safe.

The NSW rural fire service said the findings reinforced how homes in high risk areas should be built to higher fire standards as it prepared for a potentially “challenging” fire season.

More than 3,000 homes were lost across the country during the unprecedented fires six years ago that took 33 lives and killed or displaced almost 3 billion native animals.

Of the 2,475 homes lost in NSW, the research, published in the International Journal of Wildland Fire, found 94% were less than 100 metres away from flammable vegetation such as trees.

The 100 metre buffer is a key part of the widely used maps of bushfire prone land that firefighters use to plan local outreach activities, and planning authorities use to assess how bushfire-resistant new homes and renovations should be.

Associate Prof Owen Price, an expert in bushfire risk at the University of Wollongong who led the research, said the findings showed a key aspect of the method to identify buildings at risk from bushfires was “more or less spot on”.

“That’s reassuring. Distance to vegetation is really important and that 100 metre rule that they apply is pretty good,” he said.

But the research also examined fire danger ratings – an index that combines temperature, wind, humidity and the dryness of fuel – on the days when each home was lost.

When the fire danger ratings – known technically as the forest fire danger index – reached extreme or catastrophic conditions, “houses further away [than 100 metres] were burning,” Price said.

“That’s a warning sign, because we know that index is going to get worse [from global heating]. We know the direction of travel.”

He said wildfire researchers were alarmed by the increasing number of fires around the world hitting and moving through urban areas, including the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton fire that killed 19 people and destroyed or damaged thousands of homes and businesses.

Part of his own research was aimed at understanding if similar events could be replicated in Australia.

“Being very close to another house [that is on fire] is another risk factor, which is why it’s important we stop houses from burning,” he said.

The research warned that the “current regulation may become less useful over time” as the climate crisis increased the risk of homes being lost.

title: As pet population rises in Keralam, KVASU steps up dog handler training
text:
The rising pet population in Keralam has outpaced the availability of trained dog handlers, prompting the Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (KVASU) to expand professional training in canine behaviour and handling.

The second batch of the university’s Certified Professional Dog Training Programme will begin at the College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Mannuthy, Thrissur, on November 9. The six-week course covers obedience, grooming, scent detection and tracking, canine behaviour and body language, safe handling and restraint, kennel management, first aid, and animal welfare laws. Participants who pass the final examination will receive a university-accredited certificate.

Officials said behavioural problems were a common reason for pet abandonment, with dogs often surrendered because of excessive barking, aggression or difficulties adapting to domestic environments. Such abandonment adds to Keralam’s stray dog population, which remains a challenge for the State’s rabies control efforts.

Dog bites also frequently occur in domestic settings and involve familiar animals. Children are particularly vulnerable when they fail to recognise warning signs in a dog’s behaviour.

According to Sabin George, registrar of KVASU, the programme emphasises scientifically grounded training methods, including positive reinforcement and early socialisation, to help dogs adapt to different environments and reduce fear-induced aggression.

Mr. George said Kerala had relatively few formally qualified dog trainers, with many practitioners having acquired their skills through apprenticeship. The university’s initiative seeks to address this shortage by providing structured professional training.

Such expertise is vital not only for household pets but also for working dogs deployed in search-and-rescue operations. Police cadaver dogs helped recover bodies at Pettimudi and during the Mundakkai–Chooralmala disaster in Wayanad. Search dogs were also flown to Telangana last year to locate a body buried beneath the collapsed Srisailam Left Bank Canal (SLBC) tunnel, he added.

Applicants must have passed Class X. Participants can bring a vaccinated puppy aged three to five months or attend without one. The course fee is ₹40,000 and includes lunch, tea, a training kit, and boarding, food and veterinary care for the puppy. Applications close on October 31. For details, contact 9605860005 or 9495739119.

title: Vice-President calls for concerted efforts to preserve India’s cultural heritage
text:
Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan has called for concerted efforts to preserve the country’s cultural heritage and promote communal harmony, saying India’s diverse languages, customs, and beliefs were bound by shared values of civilisation.

Opening the Navaratri Sargotsavam-2026 organised by the Kesari Weekly here on Friday (October 16), he said that families, teachers, artists, voluntary organisations, and educational institutions had a collective responsibility to nurture citizens who were scientifically informed, technologically capable, culturally aware, and socially responsible.

Highlighting Keralam’s tradition of interfaith participation in festivals, he said people celebrated occasions such as Ramadan, Christmas, and Onam irrespective of their religious affiliations. He expressed hope that political violence in the State would decline, enabling Keralam to retain its reputation as ‘God’s Own Country’.

The Vice-President said festivals celebrated in different parts of the country reflected India’s cultural diversity while strengthening national unity. Durga Puja in West Bengal, Garba and Dandiya in Gujarat, and the Dasara festivities in Mysuru illustrated the distinct traditions through which the spirit of the festival found expression across regions.

“Traditions may be many, languages may be different, and forms of worship may vary slightly from place to place, but the spirit of celebrating Dasara unites all of us,” he said. He also referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’ initiative, which seeks to foster mutual understanding through cultural exchange.

Referring to Keralam’s tradition of ‘Vidyarambham’ (initiating children to the world of letters) on Vijayadashami, the Vice-President highlighted the importance of education and arts in shaping society.

He said cultural heritage and economic progress were complementary, arguing that a strong cultural foundation gave society a sense of identity and continuity while enabling it to embrace modernity.

The Vice-President presented the first Sarga Kesari Award to artist R.K. Rajendran.

Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, C. Sadanandan, MP, and former Goa Governor P.S. Sreedharan Pillai were present.

title: QR code fraud: police register case against six toll plaza employees in Kozhikode
text:
The Pantheerankavu police have registered a case against six employees of a toll plaza in Kozhikode city for allegedly siphoning off more than ₹7 lakh by diverting toll payments to their personal bank accounts using private QR code scanners.

The accused have been identified as Umashankar, Monti Rajput, Harimohan, Shim, Naveen Singh Bhadoriya and Bibin Rajput, all natives of Uttar Pradesh. Bibin Rajput was taken into police custody, while the other five allegedly returned to their home State after their contract periods expired.

The alleged fraud came to light during an inspection by the toll plaza manager after the employees had left their jobs. The police have initiated further steps to bring the remaining accused to Kozhikode for a detailed investigation.

According to the police, the employees allegedly targeted vehicles that passed through the toll plaza without FASTag. They would display QR codes linked to private accounts to collect payments from motorists instead of routing the money through the authorised toll collection system.

The toll plaza manager lodged a complaint with the Pantheerankavu police after examining the accounts following the employees’ departure. The police registered a case and launched an investigation.

A senior police officer said the amount identified so far was based on a preliminary assessment and that the total sum allegedly misappropriated could be higher. Further investigation is under way to establish the full extent of the alleged fraud and trace the money collected through the QR codes. Sub-Inspector N. Rajkumar is leading the investigation.

title: Four dead, 35 injured as Bengaluru-Kozhikode sleeper bus collides with truck near Periyapatna
text:
Four persons were killed while 35 others suffered injuries in a collision between a truck and a Bengaluru-Kozhikode private sleeper bus near Periyapatna in the wee hours of Friday (October 16, 2026).

Police said those injured, including two persons who suffered serious injuries, had been shifted to different hospitals for treatment.

The mishap took place between Periyapatna and Kampalapura when a truck headed towards Mysuru from Madikeri collided with a sleeper bus from Bengaluru proceeding to Kozhikode.

Four persons, including the driver and three passengers hailing from Kerala, were killed due to the impact of the collision. Except for two persons with serious injuries, the others suffered minor injuries.

Police said the accident took place when the truck swerved to the right to avoid hitting a tree that had fallen by the roadside due to overnight rains.

title: CPI(M) to launch agitation over ESA notification in Kannur
text:
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] will launch a major public agitation against the Keralam government for the latter’s alleged failure to address the concerns of residents of hill regions over the notification of Ecologically Sensitive Areas (ESA) in Kannur district.

Protests will be held continuously after October 25, focussing on Kottiyoor, Cheruvanchery and Aralam regions, CPI(M) district secretary K.K. Ragesh said.

Mr. Ragesh alleged that the State government had remained indifferent to the concerns of people living in the hilly areas of the district, while the Centre continued to refuse to accept the revised report submitted by the State on ESA boundaries.

The ESA notification introduced by the United Democratic Front (UDF) government in 2014 had caused extremely serious consequences for the hilly regions of the district. A ground-level survey was necessary to identify the actual ESA areas, he said.

However, instead of conducting such a survey, the Oommen V. Oommen Committee prepared what Mr. Ragesh described as a hastily compiled report in 2013. Based on this, the UDF government independently identified the State’s ecologically sensitive areas in 2014 and submitted a report to the Centre.

That report continues to form the basis of the seventh draft of the ESA report. The areas recommended by the committee remain designated as ecologically sensitive in the State and this, Mr. Ragesh said, was the fundamental reason for concerns among residents of hilly regions.

After the Left Democratic Front (LDF) government came to power, it conducted a detailed study and concluded in 2018 that the ESA provisions should apply to only 92 villages. Objections to the proposed boundaries were examined at the district level, and the revised report was submitted to the Centre after excluding residential areas and including forest areas.

The Centre, however, refused to accept the revision. It questioned how the State could amend a report it had previously submitted.

Official’s transfer

The transfer of Vigilance Deputy Superintendent of Police (DySP) who had exposed corruption in the Kannur Corporation was suspicious, Mr. Ragesh said.

The officer had entered the Corporation office and seized several documents, Mr. Ragesh said, adding that he was transferred soon afterwards as a consequence of these actions.

title: Tourism infrastructure threatens to push elephants out of Mattupetty grasslands in Keralam’s Munnar
text:
A landscape that offers wild elephants food, water and room to roam could be turning into a tourism zone, raising concerns that the loss of natural feeding grounds in Mattupetty, Munnar, may drive the animals closer to roads, plantations and human settlements, escalating the risk of human-elephant conflict.

The grasslands between the Munnar-Top Station road and the Mattupetty reservoir, under the control of the Kerala Livestock Development Board (KLDB), are frequented by elephant herds. Reports of construction of a watchtower, a roadside ticket counter and wooden fencing arrangements for tourists in the area have triggered concerns for conservationists over the impact of tourism infrastructure on this fragile habitat.

Joint inspection

ANEC Trust, a Kochi-based NGO, has urged the State government to intervene immediately, calling for a joint inspection by the departments concerned, an independent ecological assessment and a halt to further construction and expansion of tourism activities until the project’s impact is established.

“The concern extends beyond the physical structures. Construction, increased tourist footfall, vehicular movement, noise and human presence could disturb elephants and restrict their access to feeding grounds and water sources,” the trust said.

Food, water security

A senior Forest department official said the grassland and reservoir provide critical food and water security for elephant herds in the Devikulam forest range.

“It serves as an elephant passage connecting Kodaikanal in Tamil Nadu. Up to 10 wild elephants camp in this area at any given time, with prominent tuskers like ‘Hos-kompan’ and a six-member herd frequently sighted here. The grassland is the sole access route for these animals to reach the Mattuppetty reservoir. Blocking this passage will push elephants toward Munnar’s tourism hubs and tea plantations, escalating human-wildlife conflict,” the official said.

Apparent contradiction

The trust questioned the apparent contradiction between efforts to remove unauthorised structures from elephant tracks elsewhere in Idukki and the reported construction of tourism facilities in a landscape used by the animals.

“The authorities should verify the statutory clearances and assess whether the proposed infrastructure and barricades could obstruct elephant movement or access to essential resources,” it pointed out.

T.S. Santhosh, lawyer-cum-legal representative of ANEC Trust, said protecting elephant habitat was fundamental to ensuring the safety of both wildlife and people.

“If we want to prevent human-elephant conflict, we must protect the places where elephants can feed, drink and move safely before they are forced into human-dominated areas,” he said.

title: After backlash, Keralam Forest dept withdraws controversial order permitting tree-felling on assigned land
text:
Following widespread criticism, the Keralam Forest Department has withdrawn, within seven days, a circular permitting felling of trees planted by title holders on the holdings assigned to them before January 1, 1977.

Many even compared the order to the infamous Muttil illegal tree-felling case where a large number of valuable trees were reportedly cut down based on a government order, which was withdrawn in three months. Several NGOs had written to the State government seeking withdrawal of the order.

A circular issued by the Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF) (High Range Circle) on October 8, 2026 had asked the forest officers to consider the application for felling of trees on the assigned land. The department issued the circular after the title holders recently submitted a complaint to the Forest Minister saying they were not permitted to fell the trees planted by them.

The circular permitting the felling of trees, issued by D.K. Vinod Kumar, CCF, High Range Circle, had asked the forest officials concerned to check the status of the holdings while considering the application for felling the trees. The officials were also asked to ensure that the applicants were not put to any hardship and to prevent en-masse felling of trees, which could upset the ecology.

Faced with the criticism that the circular could lead to large-scale felling of trees on assigned land, the CCF came up with another circular cancelling the earlier one.

“The circular was withdrawn as there existed some legal ambiguity over the ownership of trees on assigned land. Hence, the latest order,” said Mr Vinod Kumar.

Even though the cancellation order was issued a week after the original order, the department has not cleared any application for the felling of trees, he added.

title: Heavy rain lashes Salem, Krishnagiri, and Dharmapuri districts
text:
Heavy rain lashed Salem, Krishnagiri, and Dharmapuri, and these three districts totally registered 1,156.30 mm of rainfall in the past 24 hours that ended at 6 a.m. on Sunday (October 18, 2026).

On Saturday (October 17, 2026) evening around 7 p.m., rain started to pour in various parts of the Salem district, and the rain continued till midnight at a moderate level. The Salem Corporation workers acted quickly on Saturday evening and started to remove the rainwater that had stagnated in the bus stand premises. Usually, for light amounts of rain, rainwater stagnates in the New Bus Stand premises. Considering this, the corporation has now desilted the stream passing near the New Bus Stand and paved the way for the free flow of water into the stream. The corporation workers also remove the stagnant water using motors. Due to this, buses are able to park and pick up passengers on Sunday.

In the past 24 hours that ended at 6 a.m. on Sunday, the Salem district registered 351.20 mm of rain, including 97.3 mm in Sankari, 75.4 mm in Edappadi, 31 mm in Kariyakovil Valavu, 27.6 mm in Mettur, 20 mm in Yercaud, 17 mm in Nathakarai, 15 mm in Omalur, 14.8 mm in Danishpet, 14.7 mm in Salem, 12 mm in Thammampatti, 8 mm in Gangavalli, 7 mm in Puludikkuttai, 6.6 mm in Attur, 2 mm in Veeraganoor, 1.8 mm in Vazhapadi and 1 mm in Yethapur.

Krishnagiri district registered 499.10 mm of rainfall in the past 24 hours that ended at 6 a.m. on Sunday (October 18, 2026). Uthangarai registered the highest amount of rainfall, 75.80 mm, followed by 55 mm in Pambar Dam, 50.80 mm in KRP Dam, 49.20 mm in Penucondapuram, 45.60 mm in Nedungal, 43 mm in Pochampalli, 37.20 mm in Barur, 37 mm in Krishnagiri, 25 mm in Rayakottai, 22 mm in Kelavarapalli Dam, 20 mm in Anchetty, 14.30 mm in Hosur, 10 mm each at Chinnar Dam and Shoolagiri, and 5.20 mm in Denkanikottai.

Likewise, Dharmapuri district registered 306 mm of rainfall, including 78 mm in Pennagaram, 71 mm in Palacode, 49 mm in Hogenakkal, 29 mm in Harur, 26 mm in Marandahalli, 20 mm in Dharmapuri, 16 mm in Pappireddipatti, 10 mm in Nallampalli and 7 mm in Morappur.

Similarly, Namakkal district registered 177.5 mm of rainfall, including 44 mm in Rasipuram, 40.40 mm in Tiruchengode, 22 mm in Paramathi Velur, 21 mm in Kumarapalayam, 17 mm in Puduchatram, 10 mm in Mangalapuram, 7 mm in Kolli Hills Semmedu, 6 mm in Namakkal, 5.10 mm in Collectorate, 3 mm in Senthamangalam, and 2 mm in Mohanur.

title: Telangana seeks drought relief measures from Centre
text:
HYDERABAD

Drought conditions are prevailing across 315 out of 621 mandals in the Telangana and different sections are awaiting relief measures from the Centre, Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao has said. He has requested the Centre to provide wage employment work to farmworkers and water conservation works widely under the VB-G RAM G programme.

The Minister stated that the ‘khet bachao abhiyan’ would be implemented in the State from October 22 to 30 with the national agricultural institutions and universities. During a virtual meeting chaired by the Union Agriculture Minister, he sought additional budgetary allocation for micro irrigation implements and inter-cropping seed.

Reiterating the request for 100% procurement of maize, jowar and other major crops, Mr. Rao suggested lifting of the 25% cap on the procurement of such crops under the minimum support price-price support scheme operations. He further wanted the Centre to rationalise the prices of fertilizers and subsidies.

title: Supreme Court asks Bengal to allow MP Mahua Moitra to avail circuit house accommodation on a day’s notice
text:
The Supreme Court on Friday (October 16, 2026) asked the West Bengal government to provide Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC) MP Mahua Moitra accommodation at the government circuit house in Krishnanagar, her Lok Sabha constituency, on a day’s notice, instead of requiring three to four days’ advance intimation stipulated by the district administration.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said that Ms. Moitra should be provided accommodation in accordance with the protocol and standard operating procedure (SOP) followed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-ruled State, while asking her to intimate the authorities a day before her scheduled visit to the constituency.

The Bench also flagged that disputes of this nature ought not to require the top court’s intervention through a petition under Article 32 of the Constitution, which provides a remedy for the enforcement of fundamental rights.

“All that is required is a standard operating procedure (SOP), outlining an advance notice and a nodal officer to whom some personal assistant of the MP can reach out... If mutual decency and decorum is followed, then these things wouldn’t have come here,” the Bench said.

The court suggested putting in place a protocol governing visits by MPs to their constituencies, particularly in view of the upcoming festive season.

Ms. Moitra had approached the top court seeking guidelines to ensure cooperation from local authorities and the police during visits to her constituency and while undertaking development work under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS).

Her petition cited a series of incidents which, she alleged, had impeded her ability to discharge her duties as an elected representative. Among them was an incident on the night of August 14, when she was allegedly asked to vacate the Nadia Circuit House even as a large crowd gathered outside the premises, abusing and threatening her. The petition alleged that her requests for police assistance went unanswered.

The incident was followed by a September 1 communication from the Nadia district administration requiring MPs and MLAs to give at least three to four days’ advance notice to avail themselves of accommodation in government guest houses. It further stated that allotment would depend on the situation prevailing at the time.

Cannot be subject to availability

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the State, disputed the allegations of harassment and told the Bench that the September 1 communication applied uniformly to MPs, MLAs and government officials seeking official accommodation. He pointed out that rooms could be provided only subject to availability.

“On several occasions, persons arrive at the last minute seeking accommodation, and every effort is made to accommodate them if rooms are available. However, difficulties and conflicts may arise when all rooms have already been occupied, and other persons see

title: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal announces new party, to contest 2027 Uttar Pradesh polls
text:
Former Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Divya Mittal on Thursday (October 15, 2026) announced the formation of a new political party, Janneeti Bharat, adding the party would contest the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh Vidhan Sabha elections. Ms. Mittal, a 2013-batch IAS officer from the Uttar Pradesh cadre announcing the decision on social media platform X through a video message defined three promises of the newly announced party, centered around people-centric policymaking, decisions based on need rather than identity, and public accountability.

“Common people would be at the core of policymaking and will play an instrumental role in defining policies. Our agenda would be [Jan se niti, Niti se Bharat] [Policy by the people, policies that build Bharat]. The other agenda would be to make sure we take decision on the basis of need,[Zarurat se faisla, faisle mein barabari] [Decisions based on need, equality in decision-making],” she said.

On August 30, this year the 2013-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer announced her resignation from the service in a social media post calling her 13-year journey as unforgettable. Hailing from Rewari in Haryana, the IAS officer completed her B.Tech from Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and further did Post Graduate Diploma in Management at the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Bangalore. She served as District Magistrate (DM) in three districts in U.P.

title: Bengal govt. to be custodian of ‘enemy properties’: Adhikari
text:
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has announced that the Centre is set to make the West Bengal government the custodian of all “enemy properties” located in the State.

Enemy property refers to movable and immovable assets, including lands, buildings, shares and gold deposited in banks, left behind by people who migrated to and took citizenship of countries regarded as India’s enemies.

Mr. Adhikari, who made the announcement while inaugurating a Durga Puja at Lalbagh in Murshidabad district on Thursday (October15, 2026), said the State government aims to use the revenue generated from these properties to fund development projects.

“I have one piece of news to share before ending my speech. The Centre has made the state government custodian of all enemy properties inside Bengal,” he told people at the Puja gathering at the fag end of his speech.

“Money will not be an impediment to development works in this region. We have to beautify this assembly constituency [Murshidabad] and build model villages here,” he added.

Mr. Adhikari made the announcement 48 hours after the first Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) meeting of Home Ministers held in Delhi on Tuesday (October 13, 2026).

The forum, which aims to strengthen regional security cooperation, adopted a Delhi Declaration, reaffirming their commitment to strengthening regional cooperation towards a connected, secure, resilient, developed and prosperous BIMSTEC region.

The participating Ministers called for collective efforts to combat terrorism, drug trafficking, human trafficking, transnational organised crime, cybercrime, money laundering, terrorist financing and the illicit smuggling of arms.

Delegations attended from all seven member states (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand), though Bangladesh was represented by a senior bureaucrat rather than its Home Minister.

The Custodian of Enemy Property for India (CEPI), which operates under the Union Home Ministry, is currently responsible for managing, controlling, preserving and disposing of properties left behind by “enemies”.

The CEPI collects rent, lease payments, dividends and other recurring income from these properties and deposits the proceeds into the government account.

Sources said this income may now be deposited in the State exchequer if the Bengal government becomes the custodian of such properties.

title: Left parties allege attack on bookstalls; Calcutta High Court stays previous order allowing stalls
text:
A day after the Calcutta High Court allowed the Communist Party of India (Marxist) to set up their bookstalls outside Durga Puja pandals, party members alleged that several of their stalls were attacked and vandalised. Leaders of the Left Front on Friday (October 16) called it an attack on free thinking.

However, a division Bench of the Calcutta High Court on Friday stayed the single Bench’s Thursday order which allowed the temporary bookstalls to be set up.

“To develop a democratic and free society, people must read diverse books and build diverse opinions. But this time we have seen the government cracking down on our stalls. The Chief Minister intervened in this, but this is not the government’s job,” Mohammad Salim, West Bengal State secretary of the CPI(M), said.

Mr. Salim added that no government can stop books, and that they will, as a form of protest, set up more bookstalls than usual. “The books are just an excuse; they actually want to crackdown on anything related to education and culture. They have declared war on these creative fields,” Mr. Salim said.

Kartik Pal from the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation said that their democratic rights were being snatched away. “They think books are arms. Why are they so scared of books? The tradition of reading books shall continue in Bengal,“ Mr. Pal said.

The Left parties have, for many decades, set up bookstalls during Durga Puja festivities where they sell books in line with their ideology and politics. Left leaders argue that this has been the tradition in West Bengal, where politics, festivities, and culture blend together seamlessly and co-exist in harmony.

Multiple attacks

Left Front leaders claim that their under-construction bookstalls have come under attack and been vandalised by miscreants, many of whom are right-wing affiliated.

Stalls have allegedly been attacked in parts of Kolkata, , including in Entally and Jorabagan in north Kolkata, and Kulpi in South 24 Parganas, and Bijpur in North 24 Parganas.

The CPI(M) said that their under-construction bookstall in Bijpur was allegedly set on fire late on Thursday (October 15) night. In Kulpi, a crowd shouted Jai Shri Ram slogans in front of their bookstall while it was being set up. Party members were also allegedlly issued verbal threats by the mob.

The CPI(ML) Liberation had alleged that their bookstall in Kolkata’s Dhakuria was attacked on Wednesday (October 14). Similarly, the Socialist Unity Centre of India (Communist) said that their bookstall near Behala Manton was stopped from being set up, and that they faced threats.

Left leaders have held a joint protest outside Lake Police Station to raise safety concerns with the authorities.

Creating ‘dimagi naxals’

“They do not perform shradh rituals after the death of their parents. They will talk about Karl Marx and Lenin and sell their books here and create ‘dimagi naxals‘. They harm the nation and want to divide it up, they cannot be allowed in India.

title: Devotees celebrate Durga Puja with ‘Prabhat Pheri’ procession in Visakhapatnam
text:
Members of the UTSAB Cultural Association, Visakhapatnam, took out a procession, “Prabhat Pheri”, on Friday to welcome Goddess Durga.

Starting from the Kali Mata Temple at R.K. Beach, it passed the Pandurangapuram Temple and ended at AMCOSA Hall, Maharanipeta. Men, women and children sang bhajans to the rhythm of the dhak, kansor and shankho, the men in red kurtas and white pyjamas, most women in white sarees with red borders.

Dr. Alok Mazumdar of the association said, celebrations at the pandal will continue till October 20, when “Bisarjan” will be held. They include “Agomoni” songs on Shashthi, harvest dances on Saptami, and Sandhi Puja and a concert by Kolkata singers on Nabami. Bhog prasad, competitions and a food festival outside the pandal are planned.

title: Anti-CEC protest: Farmers to march to Delhi on October 23
text:
Various farmers’ organisations, under the banner of Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM), will march to Delhi on October 23 demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Briefing reporters here on Friday, senior SKM leader and president of All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) Ashok Dhawale said farmers would hold protests simultaneously at all district, taluk and block headquarters in support of the demand.

Keep track | Anti-CEC protests key highlights

When asked about the ban on protests near Jantar Mantar, Mr. Dhawale said farmers were prepared for larger struggles. “This is going to be one of the largest struggles against SIR,” he said, and added that farmers were not scared of suppression. “Let them [the authorities] dare to do what they want to do,” he said, and maintained that students, youth, women and civil society organisations and members of trade unions would also join the protests.

Nalgonda conference

Mr. Dhawale and AIKS general secretary Vijoo Krishnan also released a logo of the 36th all India conference of the AIKS, which would be held at Nalgonda from November 15 to 18. They said Nalgonda was chosen as the venue for the conference as it was the epicentre of the historic Telangana armed peasants’ struggle. “As AIKS completes 90 years, it has emerged as the largest organisation of the peasantry in the world with more than 1.58 crore members. It has carried forward its legacy of resistance to imperialism and feudalism and the glorious tradition of the Telangana, Tebhaga, Warli Adivasi, Punnapra Vayalar, Surma Valley and numerous struggles to this day; drawing inspiration from them it has launched militant struggles building resistance against the neoliberal economic policies,” the leaders said.

They added that leaders of other farmers’ organisations had also been invited to address the conference as a mark of solidarity. Mr. Dhawale said the SKM had decided to hold stronger protests from November 26 against the proposed trade deal with the United States and the AIKS meeting would be a venue for uniting farmers’ organisations against the attacks on farmers.

“The slew of Free Trade Agreements, the India-U.S. Trade Deal are all aimed at pitting our peasants against highly subsidised corporate agriculture and their products will flood India without any import duties, leading to a price crash for our farmers, dairy farmers, horticulturists, fishers and fish workers. This will be the death-knell for Indian farmers and the rural poor; it threatens their lives and livelihoods as well as the future of Indian agriculture,” he added.

title: YSRCP office in Rayachoti partly set on fire, vehicles torched; party blames TDP activists
text:
Three vehicles were set on fire and the YSRCP office was partially burnt in Rayachoti in Andhra Pradesh’s Annamayya district on Friday (October 16, 2026) morning after a clash between activists of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP).

The clash broke out minutes after former Rayachoti MLA and YSRCP leader Gadikota Srikanth Reddy addressed the media. He alleged that the TDP legislator from the constituency, Transport Minister Mandipalli Ramprasad Reddy, was intimidating YSRCP leaders contesting the elections.

Soon after, activists allegedly belonging to the TDP reached the YSRCP office at SN Colony in Rayachoti and attacked the vehicles parked outside. Three vehicles were set on fire, some two-wheelers were damaged and the party office too was partially set on fire.

When additional police forces reached the locality, the protesters partially damaged a police vehicle. The police resorted to a mild lathi-charge and dispersed the activists and leaders of both parties. Fire tenders doused the flames, and the police brought the situation under control.

Mr. Srikanth Reddy alleged that the TDP, which was treating the elections as a matter of prestige, was trying to win them by resorting to violence. He said the party should instead fulfil its poll promises and win the hearts of the people.

The incident created panic among residents because the office is in a residential area.

title: TDP names Mukka Sravani as GVMC Mayor candidate
text:
After prolonged deliberations among senior leaders and party cadres, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) high command has announced Dr Mukka Sravani as its candidate for the Mayor’s post in the upcoming Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections.

The announcement was made on Friday night, bringing an end to speculation over the party’s choice for the prestigious post. Several names had reportedly been under consideration, with leaders holding discussions before finalising Ms. Sravani’s candidature.

Ms. Sravani is a former corporator from Ward 26 under the erstwhile ward arrangement and the daughter of senior TDP leader Mukka Mutyala Naidu. She belongs to the Kapu community.

The party’s decision comes amid intensifying political activity ahead of the GVMC elections, with nominations having commenced on Friday and campaigning gaining momentum across the city.

The TDP’s announcement sets the stage for a contest with the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which has already named MLC Varudu Kalyani as its candidate for the Mayor’s post.

title: Isolated heavy rain likely in parts of A.P. amid 79% deficit in October
text:
Rain or thunderstorms are likely at a few places across Andhra Pradesh and Yanam till October 19, bringing some respite to the State which has received about a fifth of its normal rainfall in October.

Between October 1 and 16, Andhra Pradesh received 18.1 mm of rain against a normal of 86.8 mm, a deficit of 79 per cent, according to the Meteorological Centre, Amaravati, of the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam are 85 per cent short and Rayalaseema 69 per cent. Kurnool district has received no rain.

The Cyclone Warning Centre (CWC) in Visakhapatnam has warned of heavy rainfall at one or two places over the next 24 hours in Parvathipuram-Manyam, Krishna, Bapatla, Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam, Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore, Chittoor, Tirupati, Annamayya, YSR Kadapa, Sri Sathya Sai and Anantapur districts.

CWC Head P.L.N. Murthy said an upper-air cyclonic circulation over south coastal Andhra Pradesh and its neighbourhood, which extended to 0.9 km above mean sea level on Thursday, now extends up to 1.5 km, causing rain over the region and Tamil Nadu.

A trough runs from the circulation to the northwest Bay of Bengal, according to the Amaravati centre.

The northeast monsoon has set in over the State. Mr. Murthy said that once it strengthened, moisture-laden winds from the sea would be lifted by the hills around Visakhapatnam, producing rain.

Easterly waves would bring wet spells separated by a day or two of clear skies, he added.

The Amaravati centre has placed all districts under a “watch” for thunderstorms and lightning till Sunday.

Surface winds of 30 to 40 kmph, gusting to 50 kmph, are likely on Friday, rising to 40 to 50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, on Saturday and Sunday. No warning has been issued for fishermen.

In the 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Friday, Tirupati airport, Srikalahasti and Merakamudidam in Vizianagaram district recorded 5 cm each, and Arogyavaram recorded the lowest minimum of 22°C. Readings taken later in the day showed 3.8 cm at Narsapur and 2.2 cm at Bapatla. Kurnool was the hottest at 37.2°C, 4.1°C above normal.

The rain is expected to become isolated from October 20. The Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre, New Delhi, does not expect a depression to form over the Bay of Bengal or the Arabian Sea in the next seven days.

title: Jolly trip turns tragic as five women drown in Gollapalli Reservoir in A.P.’s Penukonda
text:
:

Five members of a group of 11 women, who went for a picnic, drowned in the Gollapalli Reservoir in Penukonda mandal of Sri Sathya Sai district on Friday.

The deceased, from three families, were identified as A. Pushpalatha (29), Gayathramma (50), Ashwini (23), Shaik Haseena (40) and Shaik Maahin (17), all residents of Dargah Peta in Penukonda town.

According to the police, the women went to the reservoir to spend some jolly time in two auto-rickshaws on Friday morning. After lunch, the five women entered the waters to play and, unaware of the depth of the reservoir, went deep and got trapped in the mud. As one of them started to drown, the others made an attempt to save her, and in the process all of them drowned.

Local fishermen retrieved the bodies from the reservoir.

A case has been registered.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Deputy CM K. Pawan Kalyan and former CM Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy expressed shock over the incident and condoled the death of the five women.

title: Gandhi Shilp Bazaar in Vijayawada showcases rich heritage of crafts, handlooms
text:
Traditional handicrafts and handloom products from across India are drawing visitors to the Gandhi Shilp Bazaar 2026, organised by the Andhra Pradesh Handicrafts Development Corporation Limited (Lepakshi) in Vijayawada. The exhibition, being held at the Maris Stella Indoor Stadium near NTR Circle on Pantakalava Road, will remain open for visitors until October 18.

Around 70 artisans and handloom weavers from Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Gujarat, West Bengal, Assam, Uttar Pradesh and other States are participating in the event, showcasing a wide range of traditional crafts and region-specific products.

The exhibition features several popular handicrafts, including Kondapalli and Etikoppaka toys, Kalamkari products, wooden carvings, terracotta items, leather puppets, crochet lace, imitation jewellery and Venkatagiri sarees.

Visitors can also explore Telangana’s lacquer bangles and Pochampally ikat sarees, Karnataka’s Channapatna toys, Kolhapuri footwear, Chikankari garments and bamboo products from Assam.

The bazaar offers artisans a direct platform to market their products, connect with customers and expand their business opportunities.

Lepakshi Chairman Pasupuleti Hariprasad said such exhibitions are essential for preserving India’s traditional crafts and handloom heritage while enhancing the economic prospects of artisans.

He appealed to the public to visit the exhibition and encourage artisans, helping safeguard the country’s rich artistic traditions for future generations.

title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
text:
France awoke to scenes of widespread damage on Sunday after a day of riots and demonstrations, with shopfronts shattered, burnt out cars, charred bikes, and piles of glass and debris on the pavements of Paris.

Police arrested about 1,800 people on Saturday as some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for protests that were largely peaceful.

They were demonstrating against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings.

Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas.

In Paris, protesters clashed with riot police, who turned tear gas and water cannon on the crowds. During the day, some groups lit fires in the street and torched vehicles. At least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups.

Riot police were seen charging at one crowd in central Paris and hitting several people with batons.

Further south in Marseille, protesters broke into the city hall by using a metal fence as a battering ram. In Lille, a McDonalds was set on fire, police said, and an Apple store in the city was broken into and looted.

More than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured in the unrest on Saturday, France's interior ministry said.

Around 1,500 shops and retailers were also damaged in the disturbances, the Retail and Trade Federation said.

On Sunday morning in Paris, residents surveyed the aftermath, which included the smashed glass frontages of designer stores including Ralph Lauren, Gucci and Versace.

Shopkeepers were out early with brooms, picking up large shards of glass as they began the clean-up. Rubbish trucks worked their way down some of the larger streets to clear some of the debris.

Many shops were daubed with graffiti, some reading "tax the rich" and "eat the rich."

The BBC visited a clothes shop close to the Place de la République which had been ransacked, with piles of clothes and furniture scattered across the shop floor.

The shop's distraught owner told the BBC he saw looters on the CCTV who were in the shop for just over an hour and a half, and that during that time he saw no police in the process.

The owner - who asked not to be identified - told the BBC he did not believe any of those who robbed the shop were genuine protesters against school conditions or the cost of living. He said the looters were taking advantage of the demonstrations.

Close to the Place de la République, a BBC reporter visited the Good Vibes bakery, whose glass front was completely shattered, and the Nicolas wine store, where every bottle was either stolen or smashed, leaving smell of alcohol lingering in the street.

title: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
text:
An 80m (263ft) luxury vessel has been repeatedly spotted in satellite images off North Korea's Wonsan coast from July to mid-October this year.

What stands out is the 50m swimming pool along the deck, with a cluster of waterslides at one end.

After sitting idle for months at a maintenance facility, it relocated in early July to waters off a strip of coastline known as the Kalma Peninsula.

This is close to Wonsan, a seaside resort with a sprawling villa used by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and his family.

It was not the only large vessel on the move. A handful of others were also repeatedly seen near Kim's villa, in satellite images analysed by the BBC.

The vessels are widely believed to be used by Kim and his family. Former North Korean officials, defectors and experts say it would be difficult for anyone unconnected to the regime's leadership to own or freely use vessels of this size.

"In winter, they would keep them at the shipyard. When summer came, they would bring them out and move them to Kim Jong Un's villa or towards Kalma, and use them for swimming and recreation," says Ri Jong Ho.

Ri was once an official at the Workers' Party's Office 39, which is believed to be involved in raising and managing foreign currency for the leadership.

The wealth of those who sit at the top of the secretive North Korean dictatorship is just as hard to pin down as the country's economic figures.

The United Nations and others rely on estimates to classify North Korea as one of the world's poorest countries, with an especially large military budget that funds a sanctioned nuclear programme.

Most North Koreans, according to a 2025 UN report, live under "systematic, widespread and gross human rights violations" with total state control, widespread forced labour and chronic food shortages that leave an estimated 40% of the population undernourished.

But the regime has long been known to live in luxury.

We don't know the cost of the vessels seen in the satellite imagery, but comparable luxury yachts run from tens of millions to over $100m (£75m). Kim's much smaller, 29-metre Princess yacht was previously estimated to be worth about $7m.

While vessel locations alone cannot definitively establish the family's whereabouts, their movements - which overlap with gaps in Kim's public appearances - point to activities that would otherwise remain out of public view.

Wonsan is where Kim Jong Un spent part of his childhood with his mother, according to biographers and intelligence reports, and one expert told the BBC the city has been associated with the family since his father Kim Jong Il's rule.

A defector who served for 13 years guarding residences used by then leader Kim Jong Il - through the 1990s to the early 2000s - told the BBC the villas around Wonsan were used as a retreat by the elite. He recalls seeing dozens of children and teens waterskiing during summer.

title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
text:
Warning: This story contains descriptions of drug-taking from the start and discusses suicide

The few grains of fentanyl sit in the silver foil as a straw, held between Mike's lips, hovers above, with a cigarette lighter below. The 48-year-old army veteran is crouched low in an alleyway in Columbus, Ohio's Linden neighbourhood.

"This drug will damn near make you do anything, unfortunately," he says.

The hit he's smoking cost three or four dollars.

"You can snort too much and you can't take it back. Kind of like a gunshot. Can't call the bullet back," he says.

He burns the foil and inhales. As the opioid takes hold, he grips the fence behind him. He sways as a low moan comes from deep in his throat - he could be humming a tune.

We've spent a few days with Mike - he's been our guide through the neighbourhood's back streets. Everyone seems to know him and he's regarded fondly. He helps out at a local pawn shop and gas station, and that's how he feeds his 20-year-old opioid addiction.

Synthetic opioids are more powerful and in plentiful supply, and they have transformed the drugs landscape.

Fentanyl, which is entirely man-made, is 50 to 100 times more powerful than heroin, which is cultivated from poppies. It is now often cut with synthetic tranquillisers, which make reviving overdose victims more difficult. These are homemade threats, where cocktails of synthetics can be made in American basements and bathtubs.

We have Naloxone (brand name Narcan) in our pockets, in case anyone on our team comes into contact with fentanyl or anyone around us overdoses. It's a nasal spray that immediately reverses opioid overdoses and its widespread adoption has transformed the number of fatal overdoses in the United States.

At its peak in 2022, 110,000 Americans were dying from overdoses, mostly from opioids. The number has been dropping since, down to around 70,000 last year. But that doesn't mean the opioid crisis is over.

It's likely that the reversal drug in my pocket, which has saved tens of thousands of drug users' lives, would not have worked on Mike. Because he wasn't just smoking fentanyl.

The pupils in his milky blue eyes shrink to pin pricks. "Opioids make your pupils go smaller, but not that small," he says in a singsong voice. Even the fentanyl, dangerous enough on its own, has other synthetics added.

When we ask what he thinks his drugs have been cut with, he replies: "Xylazine, and the one we can't pronounce."

Medetomidine is what he means. Like xyalzine, it is also referred to as tranq and both are synthetic animal tranquilisers. "Large animal tranquilisers," as one recovery expert told me.

They help prolong the high from the fentanyl but are a sedative that slows breathing and, importantly, naloxone doesn't work against them. Xylazine also causes necrotic skin ulcers, wounds so deep they can make it down to the bone and are difficult to treat.

title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
text:
A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys and called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.

But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened and suggested it was part of a "coordinated campaign to smear Israel".

The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the attack on Levine was "disturbing" and "not a good look".

It was also condemned by the US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, who called it a "despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards". A staunch ally of Israel, Huckabee said the assailants must face "prosecution to the fullest extent of the law".

In Saturday's incident the European diplomats - from Belgium, France, Poland and the Catholic Church - had come to the largely Christian village of Taybeh near Ramallah.

They were there to assess the situation on the ground after almost near daily attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians trying to bring in their olive harvest.

Video footage from the scene showed masked settlers confronting the convoy. Reports suggest stones were thrown.

The Belgian authorities said a car from its consulate had a window smashed and a French mayor was assaulted. Video showed a man wearing a French tricolor sash slumped beside a vehicle.

Belgium's foreign minister Maxime Prevot condemned the attack and said Israel had a responsibility to bring those responsible to justice.

"Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," he said.

"As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice.

"Impunity for violent settlers must end. Belgium will continue to press for EU sanctions against those responsible for this violence and those who support them."

Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's foreign minister, said he strongly condemned the violence by what he called "Israeli rioters". He said the foreign ministry was in contact with the ambassadors of the countries involved.

But he added: "Without detracting from the severity of the incident, it is unfortunate that the visit was not coordinated with the IDF in advance. Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors' security."

The IDF said they "strongly condemn the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Isr

title: Several dead or injured in major fire at Canada military base
text:
Several people have been killed or injured as a result of a large fire near a Canadian military base in Alberta, the nation's defence minister has said.

David McGuinty did not confirm the cause or the number of casualties, describing the situation as "very, very active and delicate". The Canadian military and local authorities were managing the fire, he said.

Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where the fire broke out, is one of the country's busiest military training bases.

Canadian TV network Global News reported that at least seven were killed and dozens more injured when a gas line or gas well was hit during a live-fire training exercise, citing unnamed military sources.

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney said that a "serious incident creating a major fire" had occurred, adding that his "thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected".

The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) said Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton had declared a code orange, a disaster response protocol for responding to a high-casualty incident.

Warren Thirsk, an emergency department doctor there, told the broadcaster that the number of patients would otherwise "overwhelm" Edmonton's healthcare facilities.

"It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It's a disaster. It's a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster."

After the fire erupted on Saturday, it "spread rapidly due to high winds" and tore through the fences of the base, the Municipal District of Wainwright said.

The region experienced gusts of up to 100km/h (62mph), though local officials indicated fire crews had contained the blaze.

The defence minister told reporters he "cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory".

It is unclear when the fire broke out, but the district first posted about the incident at about 17:30 local time (23:30 GMT).

Local authorities have urged residents to avoid the area and give all emergency vehicles right of way.

The mayor of the nearby town of Wainwright, Bruce Pugh, said it was a "heavy day" for his community.

"We have neighbours who are either serving or former members of the Canadian Armed Forces. We're integrated, our kids play in the same hockey teams, attend the same schools," he told CBC.

While details on the impact of the fire remain unclear, Pugh said he believed this would come to be the area's largest-ever mass casualty event.

title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
text:
Donald Trump has blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September.

But Trump issued an executive order on Friday night saying that suspending some was in the US national interest, prompting a backlash from US lawmakers. Zelensky said it was unfortunate the US has decided to "completely disregard" the sanctions.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Trump's order was "an important and truly historic moment", and that the sanctions would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week. Ukraine has accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.

Since then, Ukraine's president declared it was nice to be among "real leaders" while addressing an EU summit, after Trump said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The sanctions suspension seemed to add further fuel to the fire.

Zelensky said on Saturday morning that the sanctions "could have helped enormously" and that the law was "supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end".

He pointed to Russian overnight attacks on 15 Ukrainian energy facilities that had caused power cuts in several regions and said: "Russia is trying to cause a blackout in Ukraine – right before winter."

Zelensky said it was "important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening" on the ground.

The new US sanctions law took aim at Russia's economy by giving Trump broad powers to levy tariffs of up to 100% on imports from the top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas – most significantly China and India.

It also included sanctions against senior Russian figures, including Putin, as well as Russian financial institutions and Moscow's so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels used to circumvent existing embargoes.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the suspension would consist of a 60-day pause to allow for the Trump administration to analyse the impact they might have on the US and global economy.

Concerns that Trump is siding with Russia have been heightened by disruption to a US-provided satellite system used by Ukraine.

Last week, Starlink suddenly and unexpectedly restricted the speed at which drones could fly while still maintaining internet connection. This disrupted some battlefield missions, Ukraine said, and hampered Kyiv's ability to protect itself from incoming Russian attacks.

Zelensky told reporters on Saturday that Ukraine had been told by US officials the speed restrictions were linked to technical issues.

However, he said Ukraine had tested Starlink on EU territory and found "these problems do not exist" and the system was operating at higher speeds.
